news.title: Nigeria vs Japan: Where to watch FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup final live
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Find it fast with our new search feature at Legit.ng! Nigeria's Flamingos will face Japan in the final of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup Morocco 2026 on Saturday, November 7, 2026, with kick-off scheduled for 7:30 PM at the Mohammed VI Complex Pitch-3 in Rabat, Morocco. The match will be the 52nd and final game of the tournament, and history will be made regardless of the result. As seen on FIFA's official website, it is the first time Nigeria and Japan have met at the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup and the first time either country has faced the other in a World Cup final at any level.

news.title: Flamingos captain Chidi says lifting first U-17 Women's World Cup trophy for Nigeria will ‘never be forgotten’
news.lede: ​Chidi will lead Nigeria’s Flamingos as they tackle Japan in the final of the competition at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 4, Rabat on Saturday. ​Flamingos captain Harmony Chidi has assured fans that she and her teammates want to make Nigeria proud by winning the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup title, saying lifting the trophy will “never be forgotten”. ​She made this known while speaking to FIFA.com, where she declared that the players are ready to make history by winning the tournament for the first time. ​Nigeria will take on Japan in the final of the competition at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 4, Rabat, today (Saturday).

news.title: FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup 2026 final — Nigeria eyes history against heavyweight Japan
news.lede: Chennai Nigeria will look to script history in women’s football as it eyes its maiden title at the FIFA under-17 Women’s World Cup on Saturday. The Flamingos beat Brazil 3-1 in the semifinal and will be up against three-time finalist and Asian heavyweight Japan in a bid for the title in Rabat, Morocco. “From what we saw against DPR [Korea], I think it’s the core of what we should expect more of from the Japanese,” Nigeria coach Akeem Busari told FIFA at the final press conference. “But it’s a different ballgame because, for both us and them, the game will not be the same.

news.title: Argentina handed minor reprieve in World Cup final scuffle issue; Molina’s punishment reduced
news.lede: Chennai The Argentina Football Association announced on Friday that Argentina was granted a reprieve from sanctions against its defender, Nahuel Molina, due to his conduct during the final. After the FIFA World Cup 2026 final between Argentina and Spain, an altercation broke out between the players, with Leandro Paredes punching Pablo Martín Páez Gavira, which escalated into a full-blown scuffle. The FIFA Disciplinary Committee took note of the episode and announced the following sanctions against Argentine players and staff in August: Leandro Paredes (player): a 10 -match suspension and a fine of USD 90,000. Nahuel Molina (player): a seven-match suspension and a fine of USD 90,000.

news.title: Kosta Barbarouses Chooses South Melbourne After World Cup
news.lede: Kosta Barbarouses has explained why he chose South Melbourne after the 2026 FIFA World Cup, putting his young family ahead of another A-League playing contract. Speaking to Football360, the 36-year-old former Panathinaikos forward said years on the road across New Zealand, Australia, Russia and Greece had reshaped his next step. Rather than chase another A-League contract after Western Sydney Wanderers, he weighed Melbourne’s A-League clubs or a return to Wellington Phoenix. Then he opted for stability at Lakeside Stadium.

news.title: Boycotts, bans and no-shows: Notable World Cup absentees
news.lede: The first World Cup was hosted by Uruguay in 1930 and featured 13 teams, just four of which were from Europe: France, Belgium, Romania and Yugoslavia. The paucity of European teams wasn't due to a boycott but largely had to do with funds being short during the Great Depression and the difficulty of traveling such a long distance by sea. It would be linked to a boycott at the next World Cup. Italy both hosted and won their first World Cup in 1934.

news.title: FIFA lawyer departs weeks after UEFA’s 42 questions on Infantino and disciplinary meddling
news.lede: GENEVA FIFA’s top lawyer left the body on Friday after eight years working for its president Gianni Infantino and a men’s World Cup in North America which drew intense scrutiny on disciplinary rulings. “Emilio García Silvero has expressed his wish to embark on a new chapter in his career and return to Spain after 15 years of working abroad in the service of international football,” FIFA said in a statement. As head of FIFA’s legal and compliance unit, García oversaw tournament disciplinary cases, transfer market rules and contractual disputes worldwide, and steered moving the body’s lawyers from Zurich to Miami in 2023.

news.title: Spain should withdraw from 2030 World Cup if not given final: opposition leader
news.lede: “The final of the World Cup must be held where it is fair, where it is appropriate, where it is beyond question: in Spain,” said Alberto Nunez Feijoo in an interview with Spanish television programme El Chiringuito late on Thursday. Asked whether he would advocate Spain, whose national team won this year’s World Cup, withdrawing from the joint tournament if Morocco was awarded the final, he replied: “Yes. In a post on X on Friday, Feijoo said: “You do not humiliate international football’s leading power.” The three host nations of the 2030 tournament are competing to stage the final, with Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabeu stadium and a planned 115,000-seat venue in Benslimane, near Casablanca, seen as the leading contenders.
